GitHub heading slugs derive from heading text, so adding the marker or retitling a row changes its slug: old links to RE-VERIFIED rows break to top-of-page where the banner is, while links to the 194 UNVERIFIED rows keep working and land the reader past the banner. The legend omits the marker, so the landed reader has no decoding key and a 2026-03-30 grade is presented indistinguishably from a re-verified one. Selection effect makes the failure mode systematically worse for exactly the rows least worth trusting.
summary: anchor links preferentially survive to stale rows and break on re-verified ones, so deep-linked readers bypass the scope banner

trigger: a future edit adds a row header shaped in one of six ways the awk mis-parses

Six shapes mis-tally silently: a Partial row whose TITLE contains the text :white_check_mark: counts Done (first-match order); two icons counts Done; a header with no shortcode is dropped from the total with no error; Unicode icons are dropped (and the map's own 22.3 BODY already uses the Unicode style, so copying it into a header makes the row vanish); a ### N.M line inside a fenced code block is counted; ###1.7 or a leading space is dropped. happy-path verified the file has zero such lines today (265 rows, 0 no-icon, 0 double-icon, 0 no-tier, 0 in fences), so the published 195 23 47 265 is accurate - the exposure is the NEXT edit, and the Method advertises the awk as the reproduction procedure. summary: the Method's awk mis-tallies six header shapes silently; correct today, but it is the advertised reproduction procedure with no guard

trigger: a single row regrade requires four coordinated hand edits and nothing checks them against each other
classification_rationale: The Method itself admits nothing in tests/ or CI checks the four hand-maintained views against the awk. Three of the four match today (headline bars, tier bars, per-domain table - independently confirmed by happy-path and consistency-auditor). unhappy-path reports the fourth as already divergent: caption at :1577 says 49 plugins (+2 planned) while the table carries 51 shipped rows and agents/plugins/ has 51 meson-built dirs. The mechanism finding (one regrade, four edits, no cross-check) stands regardless and is the durable half.
summary: four hand-maintained views have no automated cross-check; reporters disagree on whether Appendix A's plugin count is already divergent

trigger: a later pass emits a finding_id prefix already used by an earlier pass, e.g. restarting UP-N at 1
classification_rationale: The read rule joins all rows sharing a finding_id into one supersession chain, so a reused id silently rewrites an unrelated still-open finding's disposition history - corruption of the governance evidence record, which is why the reporter derived I2. The reporter self-mitigated by numbering from UP-16 after inspecting the ledger. Orchestrator VERIFIED no collision exists: 101 rows, 67 distinct finding_ids, zero ids appearing in more than one pass_ordinal, zero pass-3 ids reusing a pass-1/2 id. Because the wrong OUTCOME is measured not to have occurred in this artefact, the row is recorded at SHOULD rather than BLOCKING for THIS run; the hazard itself is unguarded (nothing validates it) and belongs in a ledger validator. This is not a de-escalation of a live finding - the raising reporter and the orchestrator agree the collision did not happen - but the schema hazard is real and must not be read as closed by luck.
summary: reused finding_id across passes would silently rewrite an unrelated finding's history; verified not to have occurred here, unguarded in general

trigger: reader resolves a ledger row's line field against HEAD instead of against its reviewed_at_sha
classification_rationale: Two observations. trigger: an operator reads the new §20.7 caveat and looks for the action it tells them to take
classification_rationale: INTRODUCED by this commit and the only Gate 6 finding actually charged to the diff besides comp-P4-1. The new caveat quotes the source comment verbatim, including its closing clause that operators needing at-least-once semantics should set batch_size=1 or CALL flush_all() ON A GRACEFUL SHUTDOWN. In its original home that sentence addresses a C++ caller; lifted into a capability document addressed to operators it reads as operator guidance for an action no operator can perform - flush_all() is a C++ method with no CLI, REST or config surface. The operator-actionable half is batch_size=1, and only that half should survive the quotation. I8 (the information is correct, the addressee is wrong), E3, LOW; classified wording and capped at NICE per the prose rule, since the underlying statement is true and only its framing misleads. Recorded because it is a specific hazard of the evidence-citation style this document has adopted: quoting source comments verbatim imports their implied audience.
summary: §20.7 quotes a source comment telling operators to call flush_all(), a C++ method with no operator-facing surface; only the batch_size=1 half is actionable
